section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses divergent thinking as a strategic and controlled process, contrasting it with earlier associative models of creative cognition. It highlights research on executive and controlled aspects of creative thought, referencing studies such as Gilhooly et al. (2007) (Study X) on ideational strategies and Nusbaum & Silvia (2011a, Study 2) on how cognitive abilities predict divergent thinking. The text explores the 'be-creative effect' and hypothesizes that instructions to be creative will amplify existing differences, particularly benefiting more intelligent participants due to their capacity for complex mental operations.
